content.thinking: I need to lay out the root cause, executive summary, and assumptions carefully, flagging things like whether the pre-18:04 disconnect errors were baseline noise, whether redis was truly never listening on 6380 versus just inferred from a refused connection, and that recovery was only confirmed with a single check rather than fully verified against the untested second candidate. I should keep the executive summary free of specific component names and avoid presenting these figures as if they were independently computed.

assumptions: That nothing was ever listening on port 6380 is inferred from the 'connection refused' log lines; the cache process's actual listening configuration was not independently inspected.
Recovery is attributed to the rollback because the service returned to baseline on the first health check after it; no other change was ruled in or out during that minute.
The ClientDisconnected account-page errors present at 18:02-18:03, before the deploy, are treated as pre-existing background noise rather than an early symptom; this was not separately verified.

The alternative explanation - that the dependency owned by checkout-platform stopped accepting connections for its own reasons - was never tested, and is set aside only because the deploy timing and the port value in the diff explain the symptom directly.
Impact is assumed to be confined to account-page renders, based on the log lines read; no other endpoint was checked.
input.executive_summary: A configuration change released at 18:04 UTC on 26 September 2026 pointed the online store at the wrong address for the fast-lookup store that account pages rely on. Because nothing answered at that address, every account-page view had to wait for the lookup to time out before falling back to the slower path, so pages became noticeably slow and a small additional share of requests failed outright. The slow behaviour lasted from 18:04 to 18:10 UTC and affected shoppers loading their account page; other parts of the site were not implicated. Monitoring alerted at 18:09, an automated investigation tied the slowdown to the release within a minute, and the release was rolled back, after which the service returned to its normal speed and error levels. A draft code change was afterwards opened to prevent a recurrence.
input.root_cause: The 18:04 production deploy of io-shop shipped a change to deploy/values-production.yaml that moved the summary-cache endpoint from port 6379 to 6380; nothing was listening on 6380, so every lookup to cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 was refused, the cache hit ratio fell to zero, and each account-page render waited out its cache-lookup timeout before falling back, driving p50 latency from roughly 26ms to 180-190ms and lifting the error rate. Application code was unchanged - only the config value was wrong - and rolling the deployment back to the prior revision restored baseline.
